chapter: Bands, leaders and radio of the thirties and forties
title: Why Morehouse left Specht in 1924
summary: Hutto explains he left Specht in fall 1924 because Specht left sidemen to lead the band, which Morehouse disliked.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I guess Chauncey was first associated with Morgan in the Specht band?
And as Chauncey tells it on I think Doc Ryker's tape, Morgan called on Chauncey to get him to go with the Goldkette band.
Uh huh, yeah, he told us that. Right. He's the reason he went there. Okay. Why did the Specht band break up?
Yeah, why did it break up?
I don't know why it broke up.
I think you'll find on the tape when we talked to Chauncey, the band did continue. Chauncey left the Specht band I think in the fall of 1924.

Because as he said, Specht spent less time on the bandstand and had other people, sidemen lead it, including Chauncey. And Chauncey didn't care for that. So he left the Specht band about the time that Smeck had come in. I think Charlie Spivak came in the band shortly after Chauncey left.
And one of the reasons you left though is you didn't want to lead and you didn't like the idea of other people leading.
